en klovn.explanation: "En klovn" means "a clown". In a different meaning, it describes a person who acts foolishly: "Stop med at være en klovn" (Stop being a clown).

en klub.explanation: "En klub" means "a club", as in a group of people. To say you join one, use "at melde sig ind i" (to join): "Jeg melder mig ind i en klub" (I join a club).

en klud.explanation: "En klud" means "a cloth / rag". For drying plates, use "et viskestykke" (a dish towel): "Jeg tørrer tallerkenen med et viskestykke" (I dry the plate with a dish towel).

en klump.explanation: "En klump" means "a lump". To say a smooth mix has lumps in it, use the plural: "Der er klumper i saucen" (There are lumps in the sauce).

en kløver.explanation: "En kløver" means "a clover". To name a clover with four leaves, use "en firkløver" (a four-leaf clover). In a card game, "kløver" is also the suit of clubs: "Hvem har kløver es?" (Who has the ace of clubs?)

en knage.explanation: "En knage" means "a coat hook". To tell someone to hang a coat up, say: "Hæng jakken på knagen" (Hang the jacket on the hook).

en knallert.explanation: "En knallert" means "a moped". In Denmark, a moped with a top speed of 45 km/h is called "en knallert 45".

en knap.explanation: "En knap" means "a button". In a different meaning, the word "knap" without "en" means "barely": "Jeg har knap nok tid" (I barely have time).

en knibe.explanation: "I knibe" means "in a fix". To say someone gets into trouble, use "komme i knibe" (to get into trouble): "Han kommer i knibe, hvis han glemmer det" (He will be in trouble if he forgets it). To say you help someone out, use "hjælpe en ud af knibe" (to help someone out of a fix): "Jeg hjælper dig ud af knibe" (I will help you out of a fix).

en kniv.explanation: "En kniv" means "a knife". To say you eat with cutlery, put "kniv" before "gaffel" (fork): "Jeg spiser med kniv og gaffel" (I eat with a knife and fork).

en knivspids.explanation: "En knivspids" means "a pinch", as in a small amount. It is built from "en kniv" (a knife) and "en spids" (a tip). To name what the pinch is made of, put the ingredient straight after it, with no word for "of": "en knivspids kanel" (a pinch of cinnamon).

en knogle.explanation: "En knogle" means "a bone". To say someone has broken a bone, use "at brække" (to break): "Han har brækket en knogle i foden" (He has broken a bone in his foot).

en knop.explanation: "En knop" means "a bud". Do not mix it up with "en knap" (a button): "Der mangler en knap på jakken" (A button is missing on the jacket).

en knude.explanation: "En knude" means "a knot". To say your hair is tangled, use: "en knude i håret" (a knot in the hair). In a different meaning, a tight spot in a muscle is also a knot: "en knude i nakken" (a knot in the neck).

en knægt.explanation: "En knægt" means "a lad / kid". For a boy, the ordinary word is "en dreng" (a boy): "Drengen leger i haven" (The boy plays in the garden).

en ko.explanation: "En ko" means "a cow". The plural is "køer", not "koer": "Der står tre køer på marken" (Three cows stand in the field).

en koalition.explanation: "En koalition" means "a coalition". To say groups join together in one, use "at danne" (to form): "De tre grupper dannede en koalition" (The three groups formed a coalition).

en kobling.explanation: "En kobling" means "a clutch", as in the pedal of a car. In a different meaning, it is the coupling that joins two train cars: "en kobling mellem to togvogne" (a coupling between two train cars).

en kode.explanation: "En kode" means "a code". In a different meaning, it is computer code: "Han skriver kode" (He writes code).

en kofanger.explanation: "En kofanger" means "a bumper". It is built from "en ko" (a cow) and "at fange" (to catch), so it literally means "cow catcher".

en kogeplade.explanation: "En kogeplade" means "a hotplate". It is built from "at koge" (to boil, to cook) and "en plade" (a plate).

en kogle.explanation: "En kogle" means "a pine cone". To name the tree, put it in front: "en grankogle" (a spruce cone).

en kogning.explanation: "En kogning" means "a boiling". It comes from the verb "at koge" (to boil). To tell someone to bring a pot to a boil, say: "Bring det i kog" (Bring it to a boil).

en kok.explanation: "En kok" means "a chef". Do not mix it up with "at koge" (to boil): "Jeg koger æg" (I boil eggs).

en kokkeelev.explanation: "En kokkeelev" means "a chef apprentice". It is built from "en kok" (a cook) and "en elev" (a pupil). The word "elev" also appears in "en skoleelev" (a school pupil).
